summary:
BodyLogs is a simple idea: log everything that goes into the body and everything that goes out. Food, water, urine, stool. 
With timestamp. 
Without any manual input. In future - zero human-factor.

I built a working prototype. A phone on the throat detects when a person swallows. NFC tags log a meal or a toilet visit with one tap. A live dashboard shows all events as a ledger with time and source. There is also a page with a ISS real crew data. The data is based on NASA norms (BVAD, NASA-STD-3001, HRP kidney stone risk), and the system shows a warning when something goes wrong, for example too little urine.

Why it is important: in space you cannot trust your body. Thirst, hunger and the urge to go to the toilet work differently. People forget to log things by hand. Astronauts log because they have orders. Thousands of future civilians in space will not. This data helps doctors, life support engineers, planners and logistics, and nobody needs to remember anything.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

BodyLogs I/O Ledger logs what goes into the body and what goes out: food, water, urine, stool. Every event gets a time and a source. The main rule: nobody types anything. Sensors log, the human only confirms with one tap, or does nothing at all.

HOW IT WORKS

- A phone on the throat works as a swallow sensor. It detects when a person eats or drinks.

- NFC tags on food packs and on the toilet door. One tap with a phone logs the event.

- All signals go to one append-only ledger. Nothing is overwritten. Every signal has a source, a confidence and a status: detected, then confirmed or rejected.

- MFA for body events. Like multi-factor login, one signal is not enough. Several independent signals in one time window (tap, swallow, zone, later weight or seat load) confirm one event. If confidence is high, the event confirms itself. If not, the person gets a one-tap question.

- A live dashboard shows all events. A second page shows a demo crew on mock data built from NASA norms (BVAD water baseline, NASA-STD-3001 body waste values, HRP kidney stone risk). It shows a warning when something is off, for example too little urine.

BENEFITS

- No manual logging, so no forgotten logs.

- Objective data instead of feelings. In space, thirst, hunger and the urge to go to the toilet are not reliable.

- One ledger, many readers: doctors, life support engineers (water and O2/CO2 load), toilet maintenance, mission planners, logistics (food nobody eats stays on Earth).

INTENDED IMPACT

Today only a few people are in orbit, and they log because they have orders. Soon there will be thousands of civilians in space, and nobody will order them to log. At this scale manual logging is impossible, so automatic logging becomes infrastructure. The same idea works on Earth: hospitals, elderly care, Antarctic stations, submarines.

TOOLS

Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, SQLite. Smartphones as sensors and crew devices. NFC tags. ESP32. Claude (AI) helped with code, debugging and the presentation.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

- Tap beats scan. NASA already tried barcode food logging on the ISS (ISS FIT). A scan still needs attention. A tap needs less. Sensors need none.

- MFA idea for body events.

- A platform, not a sensor. Any existing device (smart bottle, smart toilet, wearable) is just one more factor.

- Non-obvious use: if a crew member starts to eat alone, the commander may see that this person is pulling away from the team.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Privacy: no cameras, only fact and time. Each team sees only its own view, only doctors see personal data.

- Cognitive load: every action must take less "brain juice" than the one before.

- Communication delay: the system must work on board without Earth and sync later.

- Honesty: built today is the swallow sensor, NFC taps, ledger and dashboard. Fusion of many factors, BLE zones and offline sync are planned.
